title: DOJ Investigates Corey Lewandowski Over DHS Contracting Misconduct Allegations
snippet: Federal prosecutors are examining allegations of contracting misconduct and potential kickbacks at DHS involving former top adviser Corey Lewandowski.
content:
Justice Department prosecutors have opened an investigation into alleged contracting misconduct at the Department of Homeland Security, focusing on the involvement of senior Republican operative Corey Lewandowski, according to sources familiar with the probe.

The inquiry follows a criminal referral from the DHS Inspector General's office, which has been examining agency procurement practices during the tenure of former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. Lewandowski, a key ally of President Donald Trump, served as Noem's de facto chief of staff while officially categorized as a special government employee—a hybrid role that raised eyebrows within the department.

Kickback Allegations and Internal Scrutiny

Attention surrounding DHS spending intensified after U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro directed federal investigators to look into claims of potential kickbacks connected to departmental contracts. The probe follows months of friction between DHS leadership and Inspector General Joseph Cuffari, who previously complained to lawmakers about agency resistance to oversight.

Concerns over contracting practices were a central driver behind Noem's removal by President Trump earlier this year. During her leadership, Noem implemented an unusual directive requiring her personal approval for any grant or contract exceeding $100,000, and faced heavy criticism over a $220 million promotional ad campaign.

Responses from Defense and the White House

Lewandowski’s legal team firmly denied any improper conduct. "Mr. Lewandowski has not been contacted by the Justice Department regarding any investigation, and he denies any wrongdoing when he was proudly serving his country in a voluntary capacity," his attorney, Adam Trigg, said in a statement.

When asked about the ongoing federal probe, President Trump indicated he had only recently learned of the matter but maintained that dishonest behavior would not be tolerated. "They’re stealing from me, so I want my people to be honest," Trump told reporters. "And if they’re not honest, I’ll have my DOJ go and do whatever they have to do."
